name: BMW R 1200 GS Adventure
instructions: omr/instructions/42063-1-1.pdf (book 1 builds the motorbike, steps 1-200; page 107 shows every function); omr/instructions/42063-1-2.pdf builds the alternate model, the hover bike, and its stand

functions.does: The handlebars steer the front wheel: the whole front fork turns with them.
functions.source: book: page 107 (the bottom left picture: the front wheel turning)

functions.does: Pushing the bike along turns the boxer engine: the rear wheel's 20 tooth bevel gear turns a 12 tooth bevel gear on a drive shaft that runs forward along the swing arm through two universal joints, and a 20 and 12 tooth gear pair turns the crankshaft, so the two pistons slide in and out of their cylinders on either side of the bike.
functions.source: book: page 107 (the bottom middle picture: the rear wheel turning; the bottom right picture: the double arrow at the cylinders)

functions.does: The front wheel has suspension: the fork is held by a suspension arm under the tank (BMW's Telelever), and a shock absorber between the arm and the frame lets the wheel rise and fall.
functions.source: book: page 107 (the arrow along the front fork)

functions.does: The rear wheel has suspension: it rides on a swing arm pivoted under the seat, with a shock absorber between the swing arm and the frame.
functions.source: book: page 107 (the arrow at the rear shock absorber)

functions.does: The shock absorbers' springs hold the bike up and spring back.
functions.skip: springs only matter under gravity or force

functions.does: The side stand holds the bike upright when parked.
functions.source: book: page 107 (the bottom right picture shows it); inferred that it is fixed, not folding
functions.skip: only holds the bike up against gravity
functions.note: unsure whether the stand is meant to fold
